key_insight: Amatlas maps Union-Find surface-code decoding onto a 2D processing-element array that runs without a central controller or array-wide stage synchronization.
engineering_relevance: Local neighbor connections and per-stabilizer memory make the architecture better suited to planar hardware than a 3D processing-element array.
method: Assign one processing element to each stabilizer on the 2D qubit lattice.
Store all measurement-round states in each element’s local memory.
Advance every element each clock cycle, with the clock as the only global signal.
evidence_signal: Under circuit-level noise, the RTL implementation fits a VCU129 FPGA through code distance 25, averaging 462 ns per round at 0.1% physical error, with a 0.72% threshold versus 0.78% reported for Union-Find under the same noise model.
watch_item: Scaling beyond distance 25 remains to be demonstrated, including the local-memory cost of storing measurement-round states.
paper_title: Amatlas: A 2D Array Architecture for Union-Find Decoding Without Global Coordination
